title: What Was Actually in Snake Oil

sections.name: What Was Actually in Snake Oil
lines: In the 1890s, a cowboy called Clark Stanley became famous selling snake oil.
He said he learned the recipe from healers, and boiled rattlesnakes in front of crowds.
He claimed it cured aches, pains, toothaches and more.
Then, in 1917, government chemists tested a bottle.
It was mostly mineral oil, with beef fat, red pepper and turpentine. No snake at all.
He was fined twenty dollars. And snake oil became a word for any fake cure.
